messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Exact algebraic coordinates from lifting a triangular lattice fragment

Generate 10 candidate conjectures within that direction, sampled from the
full distribution of responses you could give. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

message.content: {"candidates": [{"conjecture": "Place 13 points at exact algebraic coordinates obtained by projecting a 4x4 fragment of the A2 triangular lattice (vertices in Q(√3)) from a tilted plane z = αx + βy onto [0,1]² with α = √3/6, β = √3/12. The minimum triangle area equals 1/72 exactly, achieved by the shortest-lattice-edge triangles in the projected configuration.", "probability": 0.087}, {"conjecture": "Take a 13-point subset of the triangular lattice {i + jω : 0≤i,j, i+j≤4} ⊂ Z[ω], ω = e^{iπ/3}, mapped into [0,1]² by dividing coordinates by 4. The minimum triangle area is exactly 1/(32√3), attained by every elementary equilateral lattice triangle of side 1/4.", "probability": 0.092}, {"conjecture": "Lift a 13-point hexagonal cap from the A2 lattice using the embedding (i,j) ↦ (i/4 + j/8, j√3/8) with i,j ∈ Z≥0, i+j≤4, yielding 15 points of which removing the two extreme (4,0),(0,4) leaves 13. The minimum area over all 286 triangles is 1/(32√3).", "probability": 0.078}, {"conjecture": "Project the 13 points (i,j) with i,j ∈ Z≥0, i+j ≤ 3 plus the centroid (1/3,1/3) from the plane z=√3(x+y)/6 into [0,1]² via (x,y) ↦ (x − z/√2, y − z/√2). All coordinates lie in Q(√6) and the minimum triangle area is exactly 1/(48√3).", "probability": 0.065}, {"conjecture": "Embed a 13-point fragment of the A2 lattice at coordinates (a + b/2, b√3/2)/3 for integers a,b with 0≤a, 0≤b, a+b≤3, giving 10 points, augmented by the three midpoints of the boundary edges and the centroid. All coordinates are in Q(√3), and the minimum triangle area is exactly 1/(108√3).", "probability": 0.081}, {"conjecture": "Use the 13 points from a 5-row triangular array {(i/4 + j/8, j√3/8) : 0≤j≤4, 0≤i≤4−j} selecting only j∈{0,2,4} rows (3+3+2=8) plus 5 interior points at half-lattice positions. Coordinates are in Q(√3) and minimum area is 1/(64√3).", "probability": 0.053}, {"conjecture": "Apply an area-preserving affine shear (x,y) ↦ (x + y/√3, y) to the standard triangular lattice fragment with 13 points at {(i + j/2, j√3/2)/4 : i+j≤4}, producing coordinates in Q(√3) within [0,1]². The minimum triangle area is preserved at 1/(32√3) by the determinant-1 map.", "probability": 0.088}, {"conjecture": "Take 13 points as the image of {(a,b) ∈ Z² : a²+ab+b² ≤ 4} under (a,b) ↦ ((a+b/2)/3, b√3/6), giving 13 Eisenstein-norm-ball lattice points in [0,1]². All 13 points have coordinates in Q(√3) and the minimum triangle area equals 1/(24√3), achieved by adjacent collinear triples in the lifted lattice.", "probability": 0.069}, {"conjecture": "Place 13 points at (i/3 + j/6, j/(2√3)) for (i,j) in a 13-point subset of {(i,j) : 0≤j≤3, 0≤i≤3−j} ∪ midpoints, yielding coordinates in Q(√3). The minimum triangle area is exactly 1/(12√3), dominated by triangles with one point on each of three consecutive lattice rows.", "probability": 0.063}]}
